reviewer: ownership subagent, independent of capacity implementation
scope: Read-only storage.js diff review and an independent execution of 9 new capacity cases plus 10 unchanged size-boundary cases. No runtime edits during review.
findings: measureSaveCapacity calls existing encodeSave, which validates and serializes the complete state; unknown fields and the outer envelope are measured.
TextEncoder measures UTF-8 bytes, while raw.length measures UTF-16 code units. The API explicitly distinguishes both and matches the unchanged strict > 5,000,000 write boundary.

The new diagnostic neither calls storage nor changes encodeSave/decodeSave export and rescue compatibility. Historically readable multibyte exports remain encodable and measurable even when new writes exceed the byte limit.

saveGame retains full expected comparison before size checks and archives; size rejection precedes archive/main/mirror writes. saveImportedGame retains exact raw/imported equality and pre-archive final-size rejection.
Primary and mirror order is unchanged. The diagnostic does not claim browser quota availability; primary-failure and mirror-failure outcomes remain separate.
Original byte-boundary regressions still cover same-revision expected conflicts, stale-expected priority, V4 migration growth, full unknown metadata and no-write failures.
nonBlockingFollowup: UI should invoke capacity checks on request and invalidate cached results when the observed save changes; UI integration and browser verification are owned by the parent agent.
limitations: No physical browser storage quota measurement in this subtask.
A capacity diagnostic describes the inspected snapshot; later growing actions remain subject to normal save rejection.
